form.zh: 七言古诗（前六句为五言）
form.en: old-style poem, six five-character lines then six seven-character lines

text_note.zh: 第七、八句原始资料作“黄云陇底白雪飞，未得报恩不能归”，通行本（如《唐诗三百首》）作“黄云陇底白云飞，未得报恩不得归”，这里从通行本。第十一句原始资料的“羗”是“羌”的异体字。
text_note.en: In lines 7 and 8 the source has "white snow flies" and "cannot go home". Common editions such as Three Hundred Tang Poems have "white clouds fly" and "may not go home". The common text is used here. In line 11 the source writes "Qiang" with a rare variant form of the character.

readings.en: Shào xiǎo means young, so it is read shào.

readings.zh: “幽燕”是地名，读 yān，不读 yàn。
readings.en: In the place name Youyan it is read yān, not yàn.

readings.zh: “磔”读 zhé，意思是张开、竖起来。
readings.en: This character is read zhé and means to stick out.

readings.zh: 这里是“懂得、会”的意思，读 jiě。
readings.en: Here it means to know how to, read jiě.

readings.zh: 这里是“做、吹奏”的意思，读 wéi。
readings.en: Here it means to play or make a sound, read wéi.

glosses.zh: 事长征：去远方打仗。事，从事、去做。
glosses.en: shì cháng zhēng: to go to war far away.

glosses.zh: 幽燕：古代幽州和燕国一带，在今天的河北北部和辽宁一带，那里的人以勇猛出名。
glosses.en: Yōu Yān: the old regions of Youzhou and Yan, in today's northern Hebei and Liaoning. People there were known for being brave and fierce.

glosses.zh: 客：这里指出门在外的人，也有游侠的意思。
glosses.en: kè: a person far from home, here a wandering warrior.
dǔ shèng: to compete to see who wins.

glosses.zh: 轻七尺：看轻自己的身体，不怕死。七尺，古人说男子身高七尺，指身体。
glosses.en: qīng qī chǐ: to care little for his own body, not to fear death. Seven chi was said to be a grown man's height, so it means the body.
mò gǎn qián: no one dares come near.

glosses.zh: 猬毛磔：像刺猬的刺一样根根竖起。猬，刺猬；磔，张开。
glosses.en: wèi máo zhé: sticking out like a hedgehog's spines.

glosses.zh: 陇底：陇山脚下，在今天的陕西、甘肃交界处，是古代的边塞。
glosses.en: lǒng dǐ: the foot of Long Mountain, on today's border of Shaanxi and Gansu, an old frontier.

glosses.zh: 黄云：边塞上被风沙吹得发黄的云。
glosses.en: huáng yún: clouds turned yellow by sand blowing on the frontier.

glosses.zh: 报恩：报答国家或君主的恩情。
glosses.en: bào ēn: to repay the kindness of the country or ruler.

glosses.zh: 辽东：今天辽宁东南部一带。
glosses.en: Liáo dōng: the area east of the Liao River, in today's Liaoning.

glosses.zh: 羌笛：古代西北羌族人吹的笛子。
glosses.en: qiāng dí: a flute played by the Qiang people of the northwest.

glosses.zh: 出塞：一首曲子的名字，写的是到边塞去打仗的事，曲调很悲凉。
glosses.en: chū sài: the name of a tune about going out to the frontier to fight, sad in sound.

translation.en: A real man goes far away to war.

translation.zh: 他从小就是幽燕一带的游侠。
translation.en: Since boyhood he has roamed the land of Youyan.
He tests himself against others on horseback,

translation.zh: 从来不把自己的性命当回事。
translation.en: and has never cared much for his own life.
When he fights, no one dares come near;

translation.zh: 胡子像刺猬的刺一样根根竖起。
translation.en: his beard bristles like a hedgehog's spines.

translation.zh: 陇山脚下黄云沉沉，白云飘飞，
translation.en: At the foot of Long Mountain, yellow clouds hang low and white clouds fly;

translation.zh: 还没报答国家的恩情，就不能回家。
translation.en: until he has repaid his country, he may not go home.

translation.zh: 有个十五岁的辽东姑娘，
translation.en: There is a girl from Liaodong, fifteen years old,

translation.zh: 琵琶弹得熟练，又会唱歌跳舞。
translation.en: who plays the pipa well and knows how to sing and dance.

translation.zh: 今天她用羌笛吹起《出塞》的曲子，
translation.en: Today she plays the tune "Out to the Frontier" on a Qiang flute,

translation.zh: 全军的将士听了都泪如雨下。
translation.en: and the whole army weeps tears like rain.

background.zh: “古意”的意思是模仿古诗的写法，借古人的题材来写。这首诗写一个从小在边地长大的勇士，在边塞打仗，不怕死，可是一听到悲凉的笛声，也忍不住想家落泪。诗的具体写作时间不清楚。唐代边塞战事很多，很多诗人都写过这类边塞诗。
background.en: "In the old style" means written the way old poems were, using old subjects. This poem is about a brave soldier who grew up on the northern borderlands. He fights at the frontier and has no fear of death. Yet when he hears a sad flute tune, even he thinks of home and cannot hold back tears. We do not know exactly when it was written. There were many frontier wars in the Tang, and many poets wrote frontier poems like this.

author_note.zh: 李颀（约690—约751），唐代诗人，做过小官，后来长期隐居。他和王维、高适、王昌龄都有来往，擅长写边塞诗和描写音乐的诗。这首诗前面写勇士的豪气，后面写音乐让人落泪，正好把他的两个长处都用上了。
author_note.en: Li Qi (about 690–about 751) was a Tang poet. He held a small post, then lived for many years as a recluse. He knew Wang Wei, Gao Shi and Wang Changling, and was good at frontier poems and at poems describing music. This poem uses both strengths: first a soldier's daring, then music that makes men weep.

appreciation.zh: 前六句写勇士，用短短的五言，像一下一下的鼓点：从小出门，马上争胜，不怕死，杀人没人敢靠近，胡子像刺猬一样竖着。一个凶猛的形象一下子立起来了。第七、八句换成长长的七言，景色变得辽阔：黄云、白云，望不到家。最后四句忽然来了一个十五岁的姑娘，吹起悲凉的《出塞》曲，全军都哭了。最硬的人被最柔的笛声打动，这种对比让人特别难忘：再勇敢的人，心里也想家。
appreciation.en: The first six lines are about the soldier. They are short, five characters each, like beats on a drum. He left home young, fights for victory on horseback, has no fear of death, no one dares come near him, and his beard bristles like a hedgehog. A fierce figure stands up before us at once. Lines 7 and 8 switch to longer seven-character lines, and the view opens wide: yellow clouds, white clouds, no home in sight. Then suddenly, in the last four lines, a fifteen-year-old girl plays the sad tune "Out to the Frontier", and the whole army weeps. The toughest men are moved by the softest flute. That contrast is hard to forget: however brave you are, you still miss home.
